summary: Intermittent artifact fetch auth failures from dual-stack VPCE (IPv6) causing partial shard retries and 502s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 502/401-like failures during model shard downloads from S3-presigned URLs when their VPCE is configured for IPv6/dual-stack. Failures correlated with requests routed over the customer VPCE IPv6 path. Impact: degraded model load success leading to partial retry loops and increased tail latency for inference on private cluster nodes.

Impact:
- ~7% of shard fetches failing intermittently for this customer's serving fleet in us-east-1 between 2026-03-09 22:00 and ongoing.
- Upstream symptom: serving nodes observe 'artifact validation failed' followed by range-retry and occasional 502 returned to client.
- Customer-facing: short-lived inference errors, occasional degraded throughput during nightly batch loads.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC/VPC Endpoint) with VPCE endpoint for artifact proxying.
- VPCE configured for ipv4+ipv6 dual-stack. Egress path goes through corporate proxy/appliance that performs TLS interception for IPv6 flows.
- Artifact store: S3 compatible with presigned URL authentication.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Trigger model pull on a serving node via rolling restart.
2) Observe artifact fetch logs.
3) When egress path prefers IPv6 (observed in ~1/12 attempts), 1-2 shard fetches fail with auth or integrity errors and trigger range retries.

Observed logs (serving node):
- 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z artifact_fetcher.go:143 WARN fetch shard 00023: http error status=502 body=\"Bad Gateway\" url=\"https://s3.internal.redwood/artifacts/...\"
- 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z auth.go:87 ERROR presign validation failed: signature mismatch after redirect (received SNI host=\"ipv6-proxy.corp.local\")
- curl -v output captured by customer when forcing IPv6:
  * TCP_NODELAY set
  * Connected to ipv6-proxy.corp.local (2606:4700::) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake: SNI sent: s3.internal.redwood
  * TLS server certificate subject CN=proxy.corp.local
  * POST /artifact-range HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

Hypothesis:
- The corporate IPv6 egress appliance is terminating TLS and re-originating connections to S3 but rewrites SNI or TLS certname in a way that causes presigned URL signature validation to fail downstream (signature includes host and can be affected by redirect/SNI mismatch).
- Alternatively, dual-stack routing causes the VPCE to present an IPv6-scoped certificate or virtual host that the artifact validation layer rejects.

Initial mitigation performed:
- Support asked customer to temporarily force IPv4 egress on a subset of nodes (iptables metric change) which stopped the failures.
- We enabled additional logging on artifact proxy to capture full TLS handshake details for failing requests (trace-level).

Next steps (in progress):
- SRE to obtain tcpdump and full TLSClientHello/ServerHello on a failing node (Owen).
- Ask customer networking team to provide proxy TLS interception policies for IPv6 flows and any SNI-rewrite rules.
- Engineering to validate whether presigned URL verification currently compares SNI/Host from post-proxy path and if we can tolerate a proxy host header rewrite in VPCE flow without breaking signature validation.
- Short-term: advise customer to pin egress to IPv4 for their VPCE/NAT instances or whitelist artifact domains through interception appliance.

References:
- Slack: #support-private-deploy (thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C08ABC123/p1678891000000)
- Confluence runbook linked above.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer reported intermittent shard failures. Repro steps and curl output attached. Marked P1 due to customer production impact.

2026-03-10 - Customer (DataWave Health, Carlos R.): We see the issue on ~12% of node restarts overnight. Forcing IPv4 resolved it for testing. Happy to run tcpdump and share. No changes on our side recently; proxy updates were rolled on 2026-03-08.

2026-03-11 - Owen Li (SRE): Added trace-level artifact proxy logs; requesting packet capture from customer for failing window. Preliminary logs show TLS server cert CN=proxy.corp.local instead of expected s3.internal.redwood. Suspect SNI rewrite or split-horizon mapping over IPv6 path.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Priya Desai): Investigating presign validation logic. Currently we validate host header against presigned URL host. If proxy rewrites SNI but preserves original Host header, we may still validate, but certain proxies change both which breaks verification. Will propose a tolerant check in auth layer for VPCE flows.

2026-03-12 - Customer (Carlos R.): Provided tcpdump and proxy config excerpt. Proxy applies an outbound TLS interception chain for IPv6 traffic via a different virtual host. Will schedule a maintenance to test whitelist route tomorrow morning.

2026-03-12 - Owen Li (SRE): Correlated tcpdump: ClientHello SNI=s3.internal.redwood, ServerHello cert CN=proxy.corp.local. Proxy performs full TLS termination and re-originates to backend. This confirms SNI/certname substitution. Temporary workaround (force IPv4) recommended until policy change or auth logic change is deployed.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Failures only occur when egress chooses IPv6 path through corporate TLS-inspecting appliance. Appliance terminates TLS and re-originates connections using proxy cert (CN=proxy.corp.local).
- Presigned URL verification fails because downstream validation sees the proxy host/cert and an upstream redirect that modifies Host header or presents a different authority.
- Forcing IPv4 bypasses the IPv6-only interception route and restores successful fetches.
- No evidence of serving-runtime bug; root cause is egress interception + presign host-binding semantics.

Actionable items:
1) Short-term: customer to pin egress to IPv4 for artifact fetch traffic or whitelist artifact domains from TLS interception for IPv6 flows. (Customer agreed to test whitelist.)
2) Medium-term: engineering to add a VPCE-side tolerant presign validation mode that accepts trusted proxy re-origination when VPCE configured (opt-in) and only after cryptographic verification of backend authenticity (PR raised: infra#4921)
3) Docs: update Private Deploy networking guide with IPv6/TLS interception caveats and recommended whitelist entries.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer forced IPv4 egress for artifact fetches; failures stopped for test nodes. Customer scheduled a maintenance window to whitelist artifact domains through their IPv6 inspection appliance.
Planned fix: Engineering to implement an opt-in presigned-url tolerant validation for VPCE deployments that accounts for known company-managed TLS inspection behavior; will include safeguards so we do not weaken security for hosted customers. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4921 created; target rollout to staging 2026-03-20.
Ticket remains open until customer confirms whitelist successful across fleet and infra fix is validated. Follow-up tasks: update confluence runbook and notify sales/onsite SE (linked in comments).
